title: refuses a named_absent text that is carried
why: A named_absent entry no longer held to being absent: once the archive carries the text, the reason recorded for owing nothing stays in the pins unread, and the new release passes without anyone rereading the list.

title: looks for Tcl/Tk's binaries in site-packages too
why: The guard on Tcl/Tk's binaries gone: one left under a name the strip does not know, or among a package's files, ships again, code the app never loads under advisories nothing watches.

title: refuses a runtime that still carries Tcl/Tk
why: The guard no longer mirrors the strip: a folder of Tcl's scripts the strip should have removed, lib/tcl9.0 or tcl/, passes because no binary sits in it.

title: looks for Tcl/Tk's binaries in site-packages too
why: Tcl's thread library, libthread3.0.6.dylib, let through: its name begins with neither tcl nor tk, so only this alternative names it.

title: passes what only shares a name
why: The guard holding site-packages to the strip's names, which the strip leaves alone there: Pillow's PIL/_tkinter_finder.py would refuse every runtime that carried Pillow.

title: refuses a runtime that still carries Tcl/Tk
why: Windows' zlib1.dll let through in the runtime's own DLLs: it is the one file of the strip that is not named for Tcl or Tk, and the zlib OSV reports advisories against.

title: refuses a runtime that still carries Tcl/Tk
why: The vendor job's check no longer asks about Tcl/Tk: --packages is the one check vendor-python.sh makes after the strip, so a strip that missed something would be found only at packaging, after the artefact was uploaded.

title: never calls clean a runtime it could not read whole
why: A folder the guard could not list counted as one holding nothing, so a runtime it never saw, or never found, passed as stripped.

title: refuses a macOS build that links a zlib of its own
why: A macOS build linking a zlib of its own passes: the runtime then ships a zlib whose version the pins do not record and the vulnerability watch never asks about.

title: refuses a macOS build that links a zlib of its own
why: A macOS build whose metadata names no zlib link at all passes, as a zlib compiled into the interpreter would read, and the watch's SYSTEM_ZLIB goes on assuming the system's.

title: refuses a macOS build that links a zlib of its own
why: The macOS zlib tripwire written but never asked: neither the vendor job's licence check nor the packaging check would notice a build that stopped linking the system's libz.
